title: Comparison Between Statistical Model and Machine Learning Methods for Predicting the Risk of Renal Function Decline Using Routine Clinical Data in Health Screening.
summary: A retrospective 2166-person screening cohort used seven machine-learning models to predict renal-function decline; gradient boosting reached AUROC 0.914 versus 0.882 for logistic regression, with bounded held-out validation.
ai_technology: Materials and Methods define seven ML models and the 80/20 repeated split.
organization: Health Management Center, The Third Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan, People's Republic of China

evidence.tested: A retrospective 2166-person screening cohort used seven machine-learning models to predict renal-function decline; gradient boosting reached AUROC 0.914 versus 0.882 for logistic regression, with bounded held-out validation.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the reported models, cohorts, datasets or experiments; broader generalization and clinical or operational benefit were not established.
